verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential mechanism by which Tadalafil may interact with Pde11a, mediated through Vardenafil. Both Tadalafil and Vardenafil are phosphodiesterase inhibitors, which are known to modulate intracellular cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) levels. This class of compounds is associated with the inhibition of Pde11a, a member of the PDE1 family, which is involved in the regulation of cGMP. The observed relationship between Tadalafil and Pde11a is supported by the shared pathway involving Vardenafil, which binds to Pde11a and is causally linked to the development of Arteritic Anterior Ischaemic Optic Neuropathy and Aion. The low common ancestor of Tadalafil and Vardenafil, both belonging to the Cgmp Phosphodiesterase Inhibitor and Organonitrogen Heterocyclic Compound classes, reinforces the biochemical similarity and suggests a shared mechanism of action. The evidence supports a direct interaction between Tadalafil and Pde11a, likely through the inhibition of Pde11a, which may contribute to the pathophysiology of the conditions mentioned.
